newsitem.title: UK: Two UK Tory Eurosceptics to stay in party.
newsitem.headline: Two UK Tory Eurosceptics to stay in party.

text.p: Two leading Conservative Eurosceptic MPs said on Monday they had no plans to quit the parliamentary party because of their disappointment over Prime Minister John Major's reiteration of his wait-and-see policy on a single European currency.

"It would be pointless for us to do that," Teresa Gorman told a news conference where she announced plans to bring forward a parliamentary bill to allow Britons a referendum on whether the country should leave the European Union.
"I don't think there is any point in this kind of gesture at all," Gorman added. She claimed her bill, to be voted on January 21, was a unifying measure for the Conservatives.
John Wilkinson, another member of Eurosceptic group, also said it would be futile to stalk out of the party.
"I don't see why you should imagine we should contemplate it," he told the news conference said.
Sir Teddy Taylor, the third Eurosceptic who attended the news conference, did not answer the question.
